project.researchNotes: Sequential place 7 of 8. Strict settlement merit, See, café-led Eat, all named trail providers, picnic, public visitor parking, public toilets, access, transport, dogs and complete local HES/NRHE construction dates were checked before continuing. The Ship Inn is meal-led and removed from Eat. The Mirador at Elie Holiday Park is outside the strict Elie settlement boundary. Ardross Farm and Bowhouse remain separate.

touristAppeal.label: Strong Destination
touristAppeal.summary: Elie remains a strong coastal destination for its harbour, beach, lighthouse, Lady’s Tower, water activities, coastal walking and live joint Treasure Trail. Its Eat list now contains only deli, bakery and café-led daytime stops.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Elie’s outdoor landmarks and several food stops work well with a dog, but seasonal controls apply on the main harbour beach, shore wildlife needs close control, the harbour has open-water and operational hazards, and not every indoor stop admits pets. Those limits reduce—not increase—the visitor score by five points.

visitorHighlights.name: Elie Harbour and Beach
visitorHighlights.reason: Elie’s broad sandy beach, compact working harbour and water activity make a complete coastal visit.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air beach and harbour; daylight recommended. Seasonal lifeguard cover only.
visitorHighlights.admission: Free beach and harbour visit; parking and booked activities cost extra.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A deep, highly legible seaside experience with strong facilities; reduced slightly for seasonal services, working-harbour hazards and variable watersports availability.

visitorHighlights.name: Elie Ness, Lady’s Tower and Ruby Bay
visitorHighlights.reason: Ruby Bay, Lady’s Tower and the lighthouse form an unusually rewarding short headland circuit.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air coast and landmarks; daylight and suitable weather recommended.
visitorHighlights.sourceName: Fife Council and Historic Environment Scotland

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Excellent scenery and distinctive landmarks in a coherent free walk; reduced for exposed shore terrain, no interiors and wildlife sensitivity.

features.fullDescription: Circa 1860/70. Sizable mid Victorian free Renaissance villa set back from street, 2-storey and attic, fine polished ashlar front with raised quoins and margins. L-plan front. Advanced piended section on right with 2-storey 3-light canted bay with segmental tympana at lintels. Single storey porch in re-entrant angle with segmentally arched bipartite, door on flank with semicircular fanlight. attractionGuide.headline: Make the beach and harbour your base
attractionGuide.intro: Walk the sand, watch the working harbour and book only the water activities the operator currently confirms.

features.name: Liberty House, Liberty, Elie
features.fullDescription: 18th century, much added to at rear. 2-storey rendered and lined out as ashlar with painted margins. 3-window front with earlier 19th century broad single storey droved ashlar porch between right hand windows, tripartite with moulded wooden mullions, door on flank low pitched roof with curvilinear barge boards, pendant and finial. Otherwise reglazed, 2 pane sashes. Slated main roof straight skews and droved ashlar centre and end stacks with thin cornices. Crowsteps to rear at original north west end. Flanking walls, left with segmentally arched opening and right with door, both with painted margins, one window east gable and one window link to 2-storey 5-window canted bay at north east corner, chamfered ashlar dressings, door and finial to roof. Large rear additions. One and 2-storey painted rubble outbuildings to rear with slated roofs. Harled front garden wall and 2 square ashlar gatepiers at both foot and vehicle entrances.
